name: Jordan
sales_role: champion — must be convinced first; pitches tool to CEO and CFO
role: Head of DC Development / Infrastructure Strategy Analyst / DC Investment Analyst. Senior IC. Owns the analysis, presents directly to CEO. Direct user of the tool. The adoption path runs through Jordan — if Jordan is not convinced, no sale happens.
what_they_need_from_dc_siting: Ranked EU zones with per-dimension scores, zone-level carbon data, supply mix (grid/PPA/on-site), and energy cost differential — in one structured output the CEO can act on and the CFO can plug into a model without Jordan reformatting anything.
why_they_must_be_convinced_first: Jordan runs the analysis. If the tool does not save them hours and produce IC-ready output, they will not advocate for it upward. Jordan is the credibility bridge — CEO and CFO trust Jordan's recommendation of the tool, not a vendor pitch.
approval_trigger: Tool returns ≥3 ranked sites in <30s citing real, auditable sources. Single output serves CEO narrative and CFO cost delta without extra work. Re-runs instantly for different MW or carbon ceiling. Jordan can walk into the CEO meeting knowing CFO has already seen consistent numbers.
block_trigger: Carbon data country-averaged — cannot answer ESG Officer's zone-level questions. Output requires manual reformatting before the CEO meeting. Too slow or brittle under deadline pressure. Jordan cannot explain the scoring methodology if the CEO asks.

name: CEO / C-Suite
sales_role: buyer — approves purchase after Jordan pitches; approves the siting decision the tool informs
role: Chief Executive Officer / Chief Strategy Officer / VP Infrastructure. Decision maker. Jordan presents to them — both the tool pitch and the eventual DC siting recommendation. Does not run the tool. Pays for it.
what_they_need_from_dc_siting: Clear winner with plain rationale. Carbon compliance as gCO₂/kWh vs. stated RE100 / net-zero target — a number. Cost advantage of chosen site over alternatives in €, not rank. Top risk per site bounded as a range, not a label. Confidence that Jordan and CFO are aligned before the room.
why_jordan_pitches_to_them: CEO approves the tool purchase budget. Jordan pitches the tool as a capability investment: faster pre-feasibility, defensible IC memos, competitive speed advantage. CEO approves when Jordan shows the output and the time saving is obvious.
approval_trigger: Jordan demo shows output in <30s that is already IC-presentable. Speed advantage vs. current consultant process is explicit. ESG narrative is citable. CFO has already seen the cost-differential section and signed off.
block_trigger: Output looks like another dashboard they won't read. Jordan and CFO present different figures. Carbon compliance stated qualitatively. Tool produces analysis but not a decision — trade-offs buried, no clear winner surfaced.

name: CFO
sales_role: buyer — co-approves purchase with CEO; validates financial output from tool
role: Chief Financial Officer / IC Member / Head of Real Estate Finance. Pulled in by Jordan — not a direct user of the tool. Advises CEO on whether the financial case holds. Co-approves the tool purchase when Jordan shows the cost-differential output is directly pluggable into their model.
what_they_need_from_dc_siting: Energy cost differential between sites in €/MWh annualised at target MW. NPV of location choice over asset life (15–25 yr). PPA discount vs. day-ahead spot quantified in €/MWh — not flagged. Carbon cost delta as €/yr (intensity delta × EU ETS price × annual MWh). Congestion risk as ±€/MWh opex variance range.
why_jordan_pitches_to_them: CFO approves the budget alongside CEO. Jordan pitches by showing the cost-differential output section: 'this is what you currently have to ask me to calculate manually each deal — now it's in every query output, already in the format you plug into the model.' CFO approves when the numbers are pluggable and scoped as differential only.
approval_trigger: Location choice expressed as a € value over 20 years, not a rank. PPA discount quantified and sourced. Carbon delta in €/yr. Output explicitly additive differential — no total cost claimed. Figures consistent with Jordan's technical narrative.
block_trigger: PPA flagged but not priced. Congestion risk labelled, not numbered. Carbon intensity not converted to €/yr exposure. CFO has to call Jordan to extract the number they need — tool did not eliminate the coordination step.

name: ESG Officer
sales_role: output validator — reviews carbon output from tool after purchase; growing veto power on the siting decision
role: Responsible for Scope 2 carbon commitments, LP ESG reporting, RE100/SBTi targets. Reviews the carbon dimension of Jordan's siting recommendation. Does not approve the tool purchase — but can block a siting decision if carbon claims are not audit-ready.
what_they_need_from_dc_siting: Carbon intensity per site in gCO₂/kWh sourced from Ember, datestamped, zone-level not country-average. PPA / Guarantee of Origin pathway for Scope 2 matching. Curtailment-zone PPA with physical additionality argument. Output audit-ready for LP carbon reporting.
approval_trigger: Carbon below LP mandate ceiling. Ember data cited with date. Zone-level granularity, not country average. PPA with Guarantee of Origin available in-region. Supply mix shows credible path to 100% renewable matching with physical additionality.
block_trigger: PPA in different bidding zone — no physical additionality, greenwashing risk. Carbon data country-averaged and not audit-ready. No citation trail — tool output not defensible to LP auditors.

name: Infrastructure PM
sales_role: output validator — receives tool output downstream and executes against it; flags if connectivity / substation data is unreliable
role: Project Manager executing the build post-siting decision. Focused on delivery risk: grid connection timelines, substation capacity, land title, planning probability. High operational interest in site data; no influence over tool purchase or siting decision.
what_they_need_from_dc_siting: Substation density and HV grid connection capacity near shortlisted sites. Fiber backhaul availability. Land parcel availability at required building footprint. Realistic grid connection timelines by region — not EU averages.
approval_trigger: OSM substation data reflects actual HV capacity. Connectivity score distinguishes fiber-dense from greenfield. Congestion score flags single-point-of-failure topology. Land availability tied to footprint input, not just regional proxy.
block_trigger: Tool scores a zone high but TSO grid connection backlog is 24+ months. Substation density from OSM is outdated. Land availability is regional average — actual parcel not confirmed.

name: Legal / Regulatory Counsel
sales_role: output validator — reviews jurisdiction flags in tool output; can escalate to IC and delay transaction
role: Reviews regulatory exposure in target jurisdictions: DC permitting law, grid connection contracts, PPA enforceability, data residency. Does not approve tool purchase. Can delay or block siting decisions through formal risk opinion to IC.
what_they_need_from_dc_siting: Jurisdiction-level regulatory flag per shortlisted site. PPA structure locally enforceable. Data residency / sovereignty requirements per country. Grid connection commitment type — formally reserved capacity vs. indicative score.
approval_trigger: No active permitting moratorium or grid freeze in shortlisted zones. PPA counterparty creditworthy and structure locally enforceable. Data residency requirements identified. Carbon claims audit-ready.
block_trigger: Active grid connection moratoriums in shortlisted zones. PPA structure unenforceable locally. Tool implies regulatory clean without flagging jurisdiction-specific constraints.

name: Investment Committee / IC Partner
sales_role: mandate-setter — defines analytical rigour standard the tool output must satisfy; never interacts with tool directly
role: Formal capital approval body. In PE/infrastructure fund: the IC Partner who chairs deal approval. In corporate: exec committee equivalent. Reads the IC memo Jordan produces using the tool. Sets the bar that Jordan's recommendation must clear.
what_they_need_from_dc_siting: IRR-accretive site selection with quantified downside. Methodology reproducible and citable. Carbon narrative consistent with LP mandate. Speed: deal not lost to competitors while analysis was in progress.
approval_trigger: NPV of location choice positive with sensitivity range. Carbon within LP ceiling — stated as a number with cited source. Jordan and CFO memo sections consistent — same figures. Methodology defensible under IC questioning.
block_trigger: Methodology undocumented. Carbon exposure not quantified vs. LP mandate. Jordan and CFO present inconsistent numbers. Competitor transacted on preferred site during analysis delay.

name: Board / LP
sales_role: constraint-setter — their ESG covenants, geography scope, and return hurdle define what the tool's hard filters must enforce upstream
role: Board members and Limited Partners providing capital. Set the mandate constraints the entire siting decision must satisfy: carbon ceiling, geography scope, minimum return hurdle, ESG covenants. Never interact with the tool. Shape the filter Jordan must satisfy.
what_they_need_from_dc_siting: Confirmation deal satisfies fund mandate: IRR above hurdle, carbon within LP ESG covenant, geography within approved scope. One-paragraph board memo narrative. ESG compliance documented for LP audit trail.
approval_trigger: Return hurdle met. Carbon within LP ESG covenant — documented with data source. Geography in scope. IC already endorsed. Board memo is one clear paragraph.
block_trigger: Carbon breach of LP ESG covenant. Geography outside approved scope. Material regulatory or grid risk not disclosed early — surfaces as a surprise at board level.
